content:
Reports indicate that Apple is pursuing a new approach to introduce artificial intelligence features for Chinese users: training its own large language model with the assistance of Alibaba.

According to a report by Reuters, three sources described this China-specific model as a departure from Apple's long-standing strategy of relying on third-party models.

Reports indicate that Alibaba assisted in training the model, but neither company has responded.

Models such as ChatGPT and Claude are unavailable in mainland China, making Apple's local strategy temporarily different from its approach in other major markets.

Prior to this development, Alibaba confirmed its partnership with Apple in February 2025. Recently, China's internet regulator has also completed registration for the use of Apple Intelligence on the iPhone.

Earlier reports indicated that Alibaba's Qwen model and Baidu's technology would be integrated into the localised system.

According to Reuters, it remains unclear how Apple's new model will work in conjunction with these third-party models. Apple Intelligence is reportedly expected to launch in China within the coming months following an iOS update.

On another front, Apple's significantly revamped Siri AI is expected to be publicly released this autumn alongside iOS 27, limited to regions where it is available.

Initially, support will be offered in selected English versions, while the rollout for iPhone and iPad in the European Union will be delayed. The timeline for China has yet to be confirmed.
